candidates.title: ODSC AI x NEBIUS | Hackathon
candidates.evidence:
ODSC AI x NEBIUS | Hackathon
Hyatt Regency San Francisco Airport
Burlingame, CA
**October 28, 2026 · 9:00 AM–7:30 PM PT · Burlingame, CA**
**Free to apply · Limited spots**
​Bring an idea. Spend the day building it with other AI builders, Nebius tools, and engineers who can help when you get stuck. We’ll start with coffee and team formation, then get everyone set up for a full day of hacking. You’ll finish by showing what you built.
​Come with a team, find one when you arrive, or work solo.

**​What you can build**
​Choose a direction that interests you:

* ​Agents and agentic workflows
* ​Coding and developer tools
* ​Personal AI assistants
* ​Inference and performance
* ​An open track for your own idea

​Final tracks, partner challenges, and prizes will be announced before the event.

### Nebius challenge: Build a research agent that brings its sources

Build an agent that turns a question into a sourced, verifiable answer. Use **Nebius Token Factory** for open-model inference and **Tavily** for real-time web search, so people can check the sources behind your agent’s answer.
**Requirements:**

* Run inference on Nebius Token Factory.
* Use Tavily for web search.
* Share a public repository with a README.
* Prepare a short demo of what you built.

**Get started:** Follow the [deep research agent cookbook](https://dev.nebius.com/cookbook/deep-research-agent-tavily) and claim [free Nebius credits](https://dev.nebius.com/builders).

**​What you’ll have access to**
​Teams can use **Nebius AI Cloud** for GPU compute and **Nebius Token Factory** credits to work with open-source models. Nebius engineers will be on the floor throughout the day to help you get from idea to working demo.
​The day at a glance
​*Tentative schedule, Pacific Time*

* ​**9:00 AM** — Check-in, coffee, and team formation
* ​**10:00 AM** — Kickoff and Nebius workshop
* ​**11:00 AM** — Hacking begins
* ​**1:00 PM** — Break
* ​**5:30 PM** — Submissions close
* ​**6:00 PM** — Demos and judging
* ​**7:30 PM** — Winners announced

​Who should apply?
​AI and ML engineers, data scientists, developers, agent builders, and startup teams, anyone ready to spend the day building. Bring your laptop, charger, and an idea.
​**You don’t need an ODSC AI West pass to apply.** Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Accepted participants will receive venue and setup details by email.
​*Co-hosted by ODSC AI and Nebius at ODSC AI West 2026.*

candidates.title: San Francisco Hackathon Prep and Pizza Social
candidates.evidence:
San Francisco Hackathon Prep and Pizza Social
575 Maritime St
San Francisco, CA
Whether you are gearing up for an upcoming hackathon or just looking to sharpen your coding skills in a low-pressure environment, join us for our Hackathon Prep and Pizza Social. This evening is all about getting ready to build. We will spend some time working through project ideas, troubleshooting potential tech stacks, and sharing tips on how to manage your time and team dynamics during a sprint. It is a great space to bounce ideas off others and get some honest feedback before the clock starts ticking at your next competition.

This meetup is designed for anyone who enjoys the collaborative, fast-paced nature of hackathons, regardless of your experience level. We want to keep things casual, so expect a mix of collaborative problem-solving and plenty of conversation over pizza. It is a chance to meet fellow developers, designers, and creators in the city who are looking to ship projects and make connections. If you plan on coming by, please take a moment to RSVP so we can get an accurate head count for the food.

candidates.title: Oakland Hackathon Training and Late Night Networking
candidates.evidence:
Oakland Hackathon Training and Late Night Networking
1024 Buena Vista Ave
Oakland, CA
If you have been looking to get some practice in before your next big competition or just want to brush up on your coding skills in a supportive environment, come join us for our upcoming session. We are hosting an evening dedicated to working through technical challenges and collaborative problem-solving. Whether you are a beginner looking to understand the hackathon format or an experienced developer working on a specific project, this is a space to focus, learn, and trade tips with others in the community.

We will start the night with some structured practice time, but as the evening moves along, the focus will shift toward casual conversation. It is a great chance to meet people who share your interests, discuss new tools, or just talk shop over a drink or snack. We keep things low-pressure and open-ended, so come as you are and stay for as long as you like. We hope to see a good mix of familiar faces and newcomers this time around.

If you think you can make it, please take a second to RSVP so we have a general idea of how many people to expect. Looking forward to seeing you there.
